data.description:
## Context / Problem
344 closed bugs exist but no lens aggregates them: close_class distribution over time, detection channel, open-bug age, caused_by fan-in (which components spawn bugs), time-to-close. Trend questions are answered today by ad-hoc scripts.

## Approach
Add a bug_trends lens to the rebar metrics registry (same _spec() registration pattern as gate-economics sidecar metrics). Dimensions: close_class distribution bucketed by close month; detected_by distribution (populated as the detected-by sibling lands — lens must degrade gracefully while the field is sparse); open-bug age percentiles; caused_by link fan-in per target; time-to-close percentiles. Use the registry's source/confidence labels to flag taxonomy-window skew (the pre-convention era where close_class is MISSING for 214 bugs) rather than silently mixing eras.

## Scope
- src/rebar/metrics/ (new lens module + registry registration)
- docs/user-guide.md metrics section

## Testing
Happy path: synthetic store with classed+unclassed bugs -> lens returns distributions with era-skew labels. Edge: zero bugs -> 'unavailable' state per registry convention, not a crash or empty-implies-healthy. detected_by absent everywhere -> dimension reports unavailable, other dimensions unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 'rebar metrics' exposes a bug_trends lens with the five dimensions, registered via the standard registry pattern.
- [ ] Pre-convention MISSING close_class is surfaced as a labeled cohort, never silently dropped or merged.
- [ ] Sparse/absent detected_by degrades that dimension to unavailable without affecting others.
- [ ] Unit tests cover populated, empty, and mixed-era stores.
data.title: bug_trends metrics lens (close-class, detected-by, age, caused_by fan-in, time-to-close)
